summary.title: Compiler Explorer
summary.one_liner: Compiler Explorer is an interactive online compiler that shows the assembly output of source code in C++, Rust, Go and many other languages.
takeaways: Compiler Explorer compiles source code in the browser and shows the resulting assembly output.
It supports C++, Rust, Go and many more languages, according to the page description.
The listing notes it can compare how source changes alter emitted instructions across compilers, versions and flags, with nothing installed.
The site honors a 'no-ai' directive: if the string no-ai appears in the source or included libraries, the code is not processed with AI.
summary.summary: The Compiler Explorer page (godbolt.org) describes itself as an interactive online compiler that displays assembly output for code such as C++, Rust and Go. The fetched text is mostly interface and policy content: it explains that code containing a 'no-ai' string is excluded from AI processing, and mentions included and excluded file passes and library configuration. It contains few technical details about features, so this summary relies on the meta description and the index listing, which says it shows how source changes alter emitted instructions across compilers, versions and flags.
